**Avoid rendering historical snapshots during cleanup.** When an affected historical SQL snapshot has no optimized-query cache entry, snapshot loading can render its model and execute its stored Python before `depends_on_past` runs. Catching a render failure does not prevent that execution. An unreadable cache entry can also abort cleanup after the production backfill. Load snapshots for cleanup without optimized-query rendering or dependency preloading. Skipping optimization alone can still render the model through `SnapshotCache.put`.

**Explanation** The title names the main change: Snapshot.depends_on_past now checks full_history_restatement_only before depends_on_self. It is specific, short, and matches the one-line operand swap in sqlmesh/core/snapshot/definition.py.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** The whole-PR diff contains only the operand reorder in `Snapshot.depends_on_past` and a regression test for `get_removal_interval` on full-history snapshots. The reorder changes evaluation order only, and the boolean result is unchanged. The test exercises the same code path. Both changes relate to `#6121` and do not introduce unrelated behavior.
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description states the problem (depends_on_self renders the query before full_history_restatement_only is checked, which can raise ModuleNotFoundError during plan prod --restate-model), the fix (swap operands of the or so the check short-circuits), and the test plan (new test that fails on main and passes with the change, plus which existing test modules pass and which error on main). It links issue `#6121` and includes the template's Description, Test Plan, and Checklist sections. The one gap is that the unchecked 'All existing tests pass (make fast-test)' box is not explained beyond the partial test runs; the author should state whether make fast-test was run or why it was skipped. The template's Test Plan is otherwise well covered, so the description is mostly complete.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** [`#6121`] The whole-PR diff (merge base to head) changes two files: `sqlmesh/core/snapshot/definition.py` (operand swap in `Snapshot.depends_on_past`) and `tests/core/test_snapshot.py` (new test). The swap makes `full_history_restatement_only` short-circuit before `depends_on_self`. The new test confirms that `get_removal_interval` does not call `SqlModel.render_query` for a full-history snapshot. This covers query rendering only. The issue also requires that cleanup must not execute historical user Python and must not abort a successful production restatement when historical state cannot hydrate. `sqlmesh/core/plan/common.py` is not in the diff. `identify_restatement_intervals_across_snapshot_versions` still loads full historical snapshots through `state_reader.get_snapshots(...)` with no handling for a hydration failure. The issue's reproduction shows that the failure path begins at the load and `get_removal_interval` call in that function. No code or test in this PR handles a hydration failure or reports the affected snapshot. The current evidence therefore does not show the stated expected behavior. **Resolution** In `identify_restatement_intervals_across_snapshot_versions` (`sqlmesh/core/plan/common.py`), catch failures from loading or hydrating a historical snapshot. Report the affected snapshot and continue the production restatement. Alternatively, compute removal intervals from persisted interval and model-kind metadata, as the issue suggests, so that no historical Python is hydrated. Add an automated regression test in which `get_snapshots` (or hydration) raises `ModuleNotFoundError` for a non-production historical snapshot, and assert that the production restatement completes and the snapshot is reported.
